one_line_claim: Peak-sidelobe rejection and worst-case single-tone processing loss place five standard periodic windows at different points, but the projection omits coherent multitone addition, local interferer placement, and main-lobe encroachment, so it cannot identify a universal winner.

source_evidence.primary: Fredric J. Harris, On the Use of Windows for Harmonic Analysis with the Discrete Fourier Transform, Proceedings of the IEEE 66(1), January 1978.
locations: §IV.A, printed p.54, Eqs. 8-11: equivalent noise bandwidth.
§IV.B, printed pp.54-56, Eqs. 13-15: coherent/incoherent gains and processing gain as reciprocal normalized ENBW.
§IV.D, printed p.57, Eq. 20: half-bin scalloping loss.
§IV.E, printed p.57: worst-case processing loss is window processing loss plus maximum scalloping loss, both in dB.
Table I, printed p.55 / local PDF page 5: peak sidelobe, ENBW, scalloping loss, and worst-case processing loss rounded for the source windows.
source_evidence.page_image_check: The local PDF page was rendered at 180 dpi and inspected directly. The relevant Table I rows read: Rectangle -13 dB and 3.92 dB; cos^2/Hanning alpha=2 -32 dB and 3.18 dB; Hamming -43 dB and 3.10 dB; Blackman -58 dB and 3.47 dB; minimum 4-sample Blackman-Harris -92 dB and 3.85 dB.
source_evidence.ocr_policy: No plotted coordinate was copied from OCR or eyeballed from Harris Figure 12. The page image was used only as an independent rounded-value audit of the recomputation.

derived_table_contract.peak_sidelobe_rejection: Positive -PSL in dB, where PSL=max outside the first-null main-lobe interval of 20 log10(|W|/|W(0)|).
derived_table_contract.scalloping: Positive L_s=-20 log10(|W at a half-bin offset|/|W(0)|) dB.
derived_table_contract.worst_case_processing_loss: L_wc=10 log10(B_e)+L_s dB. The first term is the processing loss relative to the rectangular window because normalized processing gain is 1/B_e.
derived_table_contract.calculation: A dependency-free Node audit used N=65536. Each cosine window transform was evaluated as a sum of shifted finite Dirichlet kernels. Peak sidelobe search used a deterministic 1/16384-bin grid from the first local null through 64 bins; ENBW used cosine orthogonality; scalloping was evaluated at exactly one half bin.

rows.harris_rounded_check: -43, 1.36, 1.78, 3.10; the source scalloping entry is a coarser approximation, while both routes round worst-case loss to 3.10

derived_table_contract.admission_verdict: All five points are admitted. Their recomputed peak-sidelobe and worst-case-loss coordinates agree with the inspected Table I rows at the table's displayed precision; no point depends on unreadable OCR.

visual_contract.horizontal_role: Blue x-axis is positive peak-sidelobe rejection; larger values move right.
visual_contract.vertical_role: Amber y-axis is positive worst-case processing loss; lower values are preferable.
visual_contract.point_encoding: Every window has a unique unfilled shape and a direct adjacent name/value label, so neither identity nor ranking depends on color.
visual_contract.direction_cue: A dashed blue arrow says lower/right is preferable on these two axes only.
visual_contract.guard: The closing dashed panel states that omitted task conditions can reverse the selection and that no universal winner follows.
